s: Chthonia festival includes procession procession (led by priests and town authorities)
q: The priests of the gods and all the town authorities for the year lead the procession, and the women and men follow.

s: heifer sacrifice at Chthonia uses heifer the first heifer
q: The women finish them all off in the same way, and then this fresh wonder is added to the sacrifice: on whichever side the first heifer falls all must fall.

s: heifer sacrifice at Chthonia is performed by four old women (inside the temple)
q: And four old women are waiting inside, and they finish the heifer. For whoever can get the chance cuts its throat with a sickle.

s: Hermione has temple of Clymenus (opposite the temple of Chthonia)
q: This temple is opposite the temple of Chthonia, and is called the temple of Clymenus, to whom they sacrifice here.

s: Hermione has temple of Ares (near the temple of Clymenus)
q: Hard by is another temple and statue of Ares.

s: Pluto has place Pluto’s place (behind the temple of Chthonia)
q: And behind the temple of Chthonia are some places which the people of Hermione call, one Clymenus’ place, and another Pluto’s place, and a third the Acherusian marsh.

s: Hercules brings up Cerberus (through a hole in Clymenus’ place, according to Hermione’s tradition)
q: in Clymenus’ place there is a hole in the ground, through which Hercules brought up Cerberus according to the tradition of the people of Hermione.

s: Ilithyia receives votive offerings votive offerings (most offerings at the temple)
q: and to her are most of the votive offerings given

s: Hermione has temple of Artemis
q: And there is a temple of Artemis under the name of Iphigenia, and a statue of Poseidon in bronze with one foot on a dolphin.

s: Zeus has temple on Coccygium (on the mountain’s top)
q: And there are temples on the tops of both these mountains, one of Zeus on the top of Coccygium

s: Hera has temple on Pron (on the mountain’s top)
q: and one of Hera on the top of Pron.

s: Mases is a former town (used as Hermione’s port in the narrator’s day)
q: And Mases was a town in old times, as Homer has mentioned it in his catalogue of the Argives, and the people of Hermione use it as their port now.

s: Mases is port of Hermione (in the narrator’s day)
q: the people of Hermione use it as their port now.

s: Didymi has temple of Apollo (statue erect and of white stone)
q: At Didymi there is a temple of Apollo, and another of Poseidon, and another of Demeter: and their statues are erect, in white stone.

s: Didymi has temple of Poseidon (statue erect and of white stone)
q: At Didymi there is a temple of Apollo, and another of Poseidon, and another of Demeter: and their statues are erect, in white stone.

s: Iphigenia is name of Artemis (cult name)
q: And there is a temple of Artemis under the name of Iphigenia

s: Didymi has temple of Demeter (statue erect and of white stone)
q: At Didymi there is a temple of Apollo, and another of Poseidon, and another of Demeter: and their statues are erect, in white stone.

s: Asine is a ruined town (ruins near the sea)
q: the district of the Argives formerly called Asinæa from its chief town Asine, the ruins of which are near the sea.

s: Lacedæmonians are led by Nicander (during the invasion of Argolis)
q: when the Lacedæmonians under their king Nicander, the son of Charillus, the son of Polydectes, the son of Eunomus, the son of Prytanis, the son of Eurypon, invaded Argolis with an army

s: Lacedæmonians allied with Asine (the people of Asine joined their invasion and ravaged Argive territory)
q: the people of Asine joined them, and ravaged with them the territory of the Argives.

s: Argives destroy Asine (after capturing its walls)
q: then they put their wives and children on shipboard and left the town, and the Argives razed it to the ground

s: Poseidon has statue bronze statue (one foot on a dolphin)
q: and a statue of Poseidon in bronze with one foot on a dolphin.

s: Argives preserve temple of Apollo (at Asine)
q: but they left the temple of Apollo standing, and it is now to be seen

s: Argives bury Lysistratus (near the temple of Apollo at Asine)
q: and they buried Lysistratus near it.

s: Lerna is a place by the sea (about 40 stades from Argos)
q: Now the sea at Lerna[29] is about 40 stades from Argos

s: Lerna has temple of Dioscuri (called the Kings)
q: there is a temple of the Dioscuri called the Kings

s: rape of Proserpine is event involving Proserpine (Proserpine is the daughter of Demeter)
q: near it is a circle of stones, and here (so the story goes) Pluto, after the Rape of Proserpine the daughter of Demeter, descended to his supposed underground realms.

s: Pluto descends to underground realms (after the Rape of Proserpine)
q: here (so the story goes) Pluto, after the Rape of Proserpine the daughter of Demeter, descended to his supposed underground realms.

s: Poseidon stands on dolphin (one foot)
q: and a statue of Poseidon in bronze with one foot on a dolphin.

s: Athene has temple on Pontinus (the temple is now in ruins)
q: And on the top of the mountain is the temple of Saitian Athene, only ruins now

s: Amymone is daughter of Danaus
q: the river Amymone, which gets its name from the daughter of Danaus.

s: Amymone bounds sacred grove (on one side)
q: the grove of plane-trees beginning at this mountain extends most of the way to the sea, bounded on one side by the river Pontinus, and on the other by the river Amymone

s: Dionysus has statue in temple (wooden and seated)
q: but in another temple there is a wooden one of Dionysus the Saviour seated

s: Aphrodite has statue near sea (stone statue; votive offering of Danaus’s daughters)
q: and a stone statue of Aphrodite near the sea, which they say was a votive offering of the daughters of Danaus

s: Danaus erects temple of Athene (near the Pontinus)
q: and Danaus himself erected the temple of Athene near the Pontinus.

s: Hermione has temple of Vesta (the temple contains no statue)
q: And as you proceed to the temple of Vesta, you find no statue, but an altar on which they sacrifice to Vesta.

s: hydra is reared at Amymone (under a plane-tree near the source)
q: And near the source of the Amymone grows a plane-tree, under which they say the hydra was reared.

s: hydra has poison venomous poison (according to the narrator’s belief)
q: I believe that this beast was larger in size than other water-snakes, and that its poison was so venomous that Hercules dipped the points of his arrows in its gall

s: Hercules dips arrows in hydra (in its gall)
q: its poison was so venomous that Hercules dipped the points of his arrows in its gall

s: Pisander of Camirus describes hydra (as having many heads in his poem)
q: But Pisander of Camirus, that the beast might appear more formidable and so add lustre to his poem, described it as having many heads.

s: Alcyonian marsh is a marsh (its depth is said to be unfathomable)
q: There is indeed no end to the depth of the Alcyonian marsh

s: Alcyonian marsh is descent to Hades (according to the Argives; used by Dionysus to fetch Semele)
q: the Argives say Dionysus descended to Hades to fetch up Semele, for Polymnus shewed him the descent.

s: Dionysus descends to Hades (to fetch Semele, according to the Argives)
q: the Argives say Dionysus descended to Hades to fetch up Semele

s: Nero fails to sound depth of Alcyonian marsh (despite using very long ropes and sounding equipment)
q: since even Nero, though he got and fastened together ropes many stades long, and put a piece of lead and other apparatus for sounding at the end, never could arrive at an accurate knowledge of its depth.

s: Laconia is a land
q: Next to the Hermæ comes Laconia on the West.

s: Lycurgus is a legislator (for the Lacedæmonians)
q: And it was when Agesilaus was king that Lycurgus legislated for the Lacedæmonians

s: Lycurgus is regent for Labotas (during Labotas’ minority, according to Herodotus)
q: This Labotas, as we are told by Herodotus in his account of Crœsus, had during his minority the famous legislator Lycurgus as his Regent

s: Lycurgus receives laws from Crete (according to one tradition)
q: and some say that he derived his laws from Crete, others that he was instructed by the Oracle at Delphi.

s: Agesilaus is a king of Sparta (during Lycurgus’ legislation)
q: And it was when Agesilaus was king that Lycurgus legislated for the Lacedæmonians

s: Delphi has an oracle oracle at Delphi
q: and some say that he derived his laws from Crete, others that he was instructed by the Oracle at Delphi.

s: Polydorus is a king of Sparta (son and successor of Alcamenes)
q: And after the death of Alcamenes Polydorus his son succeeded to the kingdom

s: Polydorus is honoured by Lacedæmonians (after his death)
q: And after his death Polydorus received many notable honours from the Lacedæmonians.

s: Tegea is found in the shop of a blacksmith
q: And Lichas discovered that they were lying in the shop of a blacksmith

s: Tegea is at peace with Lacedæmon (when Lichas arrived there)
q: A Lacedæmonian by name Lichas came to Tegea at a time when Lacedæmon and Tegea were at peace together.

s: Laconia is ruled by Lelex (in the earliest Lacedæmonian tradition)
q: And according to the Lacedæmonian tradition Lelex the _autochthon_ first reigned in this land

s: Cleomenes commences his reign
q: And Cleomenes commenced his reign by an inroad into Argolis

s: Cleomenes is mad fit of madness (at his death)
q: And Cleomenes after this died in a fit of madness, for he seized his sword, and stabbed himself, and hacked his body about all over.

s: Dorieus is born to the first wife
q: And the second wife bare a son Cleomenes, and the first wife, though so long barren, after the birth of Cleomenes bare Dorieus, and Leonidas, and Cleombrotus.

s: Dorieus is rejected as king Cleomenes (despite being regarded as the better man)
q: And after the death of Anaxandrides, the Lacedæmonians though they thought Dorieus the better man both in council and war, reluctantly rejected him, and gave the kingdom to Cleomenes according to their law of primogeniture.

s: Leonidas is a king of Sparta (successor of Cleomenes)
q: And as Cleomenes had no male children the kingdom devolved upon Leonidas the son of Anaxandrides, the brother of Dorieus on both sides.

s: Leonidas commands Leonidas’ 300 (at Thermopylæ)
q: and Leonidas with his 300 Lacedæmonians met him at Thermopylæ.

s: Leonidas’ 300 is a Lacedæmonian force (at Thermopylæ)
q: and Leonidas with his 300 Lacedæmonians met him at Thermopylæ.

s: Xerxes leads army into Greece (during Leonidas’ reign)
q: It was in his reign that Xerxes led his army into Greece

s: Thermopylæ is defended by Leonidas (against Xerxes’ army)
q: For Xerxes, the most sagacious and renowned of all the kings that ruled over the Medes and Persians, would have been prevented, at the narrow pass of Thermopylæ, by the handful of men that Leonidas had with him

s: Messenia is conquered by Lacedæmonians (after the first war with the Messenians)
q: And after the end of the war, when Messenia was already conquered by the Lacedæmonians

s: Pausanias is regent for Plistarchus (during Plistarchus’ minority)
q: And Pausanias the son of Cleombrotus was not king after Leonidas, but was Regent for Plistarchus Leonidas’ son during his minority

s: Pausanias leads Lacedæmonians (at the battle of Platæa)
q: and he led the Lacedæmonians to Platæa

s: Battle of Platæa annihilates the barbarians
q: when Mardonius fell in the battle at Platæa, and the barbarians were annihilated

s: Pausanias spares Coan woman (after the battle of Platæa)
q: Pausanias sent this lady home to Cos, with the ornaments and all other apparel that the Persian had given her.

s: Thrasybulus is coming with an Athenian force
q: and it was also reported that Thrasybulus was coming up with an Athenian force

s: Lysander is killed at Haliartus (in battle against Thebans and Athenians)
q: Some Thebans however and Athenians had secretly entered the town, and they making a sally and drawing up in battle array, Lysander and several of the Lacedæmonians fell.

s: Thebes is defended by Some Thebans and Athenians (against Lysander and several of the Lacedæmonians)
q: Some Thebans however and Athenians had secretly entered the town, and they making a sally and drawing up in battle array, Lysander and several of the Lacedæmonians fell.

s: Agesipolis takes over the kingdom (when he came of age)
q: And when Agesipolis came of age and took over the kingdom, his first war was against the Argives.

s: Agesipolis is successful against Olynthians (in a later expedition)
q: and led an expedition against the Olynthians, and having been successful in battle, and taken most of the other cities in Chalcidice

s: Agesipolis dies of sudden disease (while campaigning against Olynthus)
q: and hoping to take Olynthus also, he was carried off by a sudden disease and died.

s: Lacedæmonians has royal houses two royal houses
q: And in Lacedæmon as Aristodemus had twins there were two royal houses

s: Messenians revolts against Lacedæmonians
q: the Messenians revolted from the Lacedæmonians, and fought against them for some time

s: Lycurgan legislation is attributed to Lycurgus (for the Lacedæmonians)
q: And it was when Agesilaus was king that Lycurgus legislated for the Lacedæmonians

s: Spartan kingship has two royal houses Lacedæmon (because Aristodemus had twin sons)
q: And in Lacedæmon as Aristodemus had twins there were two royal houses

s: Aristodemus is killed by Pylades’ sons (according to the account judged truer by the author)
q: But the truer account is that the sons of Pylades and Electra, who were cousins of Tisamenus the son of Orestes, murdered Aristodemus.

s: Eurysthenes is son of Aristodemus
q: The names of his two sons were Procles and Eurysthenes

s: Eurysthenes has descendants called Agidæ (through his son Agis)
q: Eurysthenes, the eldest of the sons of Aristodemus, had a son Agis they say: (and from him they call the descendants of Eurysthenes Agidæ).

s: Cleombrotus is a Spartan king
q: And Agesipolis having died childless, the succession devolved upon Cleombrotus

s: Antigonus is a son of Demetrius
q: Antigonus the son of Demetrius made an expedition against Athens both by land and sea.

s: Antigonus invested Athenians (closely, barring allied approaches)
q: And Antigonus having closely invested Athens, and barring the Athenian allies from every approach to the city

s: Egyptian fleet aided Athenians (under Patroclus)
q: And an Egyptian fleet under Patroclus came to the aid of the Athenians

s: Lacedæmonians supported Athenians (out of friendship and desire for lasting fame)
q: Then the Lacedæmonians were eager to bear the brunt of the battle, being animated by their friendship to the Athenians, and the desire to do something that posterity would not willingly forget.

s: Areus led home Lacedæmonians (because their provisions had been consumed)
q: But Areus, as their provisions had been consumed, led his army home again.

s: Leonidas was king of Lacedæmonians (as the only surviving male of the family of Eurysthenes)
q: as now Leonidas was the only male left of the family of Eurysthenes, though quite an old man, the Lacedæmonians made him king.

s: Lysander opposed Leonidas (especially)
q: And it so chanced that Lysander, a descendant of Lysander the son of Aristocritus, especially disliked Leonidas.

s: Leonidas was recalled to Spartan kingship (after exile in Arcadia)
q: not many years afterwards the Lacedæmonians recalled him, and made him king the second time.

s: Cleombrotus died at Leuctra (at the commencement of the action)
q: and Cleombrotus, exposing himself too freely, fell at the commencement of the action.

s: Cleomenes (son of Leonidas) was last king of Agiadæ (at Sparta)
q: Cleomenes the son of Leonidas was the last king at Sparta

s: Lacedæmonians attempted to capture Tegea (following a beguiling oracle)
q: under his leadership the Spartans went out to Tegea, when the Lacedæmonians hoped to take Tegea and slice the district off from Arcadia, following a beguiling oracle.

s: Nicander invaded Argolis (and ravaged most of the country)
q: And Nicander invaded Argolis with an army, and ravaged most of the country.

s: Messenians killed Teleclus (in the temple of Artemis Limnas)
q: it was in his reign that the Messenians killed Teleclus the king of the other family in the temple of Artemis Limnas.

s: Theopompus was king of Lacedæmonians (after Nicander)
q: And Theopompus the son of Nicander, who was king after his father

s: Messenians evacuated Peloponnese (after a second defeat by the Spartans)
q: It was in his reign that the Messenians evacuated the Peloponnese, having been a second time conquered in war by the Spartans.

s: Demaratus was king of Sparta (and was in other respects well regarded there)
q: And when Demaratus was king and in other respects in good repute at Sparta

s: Lacedæmonians fought against Bœotians (at Leuctra, under Cleombrotus)
q: under whom the Lacedæmonians fought against the Bœotians at Leuctra

s: Demaratus lost Spartan kingship (through Aristo’s statement and Cleomenes’ hatred)
q: this thoughtless word of Aristo, and the hatred of Cleomenes deprived him of the kingdom.

s: Demaratus went to Darius (in Persia)
q: And he went to Persia to king Darius

s: Leotychides succeeded Demaratus (as king)
q: Leotychides, who became king in his place

s: Leotychides fought at Mycale (with the Athenians and Xanthippus)
q: shared with the Athenians and their General Xanthippus, the son of Ariphron, in the action at Mycale

s: Leotychides marched against Aleuadæ (in Thessaly)
q: and also marched into Thessaly against the Aleuadæ.

s: Platæa was friendly to Athenians (despite maintaining peace between the Peloponnesians and Athenians)
q: captured after a siege the town of Platæa which was friendly to the Athenians.

s: Sthenelaidas caused Peloponnesian War (mainly, as a powerful Ephor)
q: But Sthenelaidas, one of the Ephors, a man of great power at Lacedæmon, was mainly the cause of the war at that time.

s: Peloponnesian War shook Greece (to its foundation)
q: And this war shook Greece, which was previously in a flourishing condition, to its foundation

s: Philip reduced Greece (after the Peloponnesian War, when Greece was weakened)
q: afterwards Philip the son of Amyntas reduced it completely, when it was already rotten and altogether unsound.

s: Cynisca won Olympian games (the first woman to win the prize)
q: and was the first woman who trained horses, and the first woman who won the prize at Olympia

s: Agis is a son of Archidamus (and Spartan king)
q: And in the reign of Agis, the son of Archidamus

s: Agis invades Elis (at once)
q: the Lacedæmonians under King Agis at once invaded Elis.

s: Elis controlled Lepreum (as a subject city)
q: bidding them allow the people of Lepreum, and all other resident aliens who were subject to them, to live according to their own laws.

s: Agis fortified Decelea (as a constant menace to the Athenians)
q: After this Agis kept continually attacking Attica, and fortified Decelea as a constant menace to the Athenians

s: Lysander (son of Aristocritus) violates the solemn oaths (mutually sworn by the Lacedæmonians and Athenians)
q: Lysander the son of Aristocritus and Agis violated the solemn oaths which the Lacedæmonians and Athenians had mutually sworn to observe

s: Agesilaus is a son of Archidamus (and Spartan king)
q: So Agesilaus the son of Archidamus was king

s: Agesilaus commanded invasion of Asia (as commander of the land forces)
q: Agesilaus, after being instructed to convey the expedition to Asia as commander of the land forces

s: Corinthians remains at invasion of Asia (because they took it as an evil omen)
q: took it as an evil omen, and remained at home sorely against their will

s: Thebans refused to join invasion of Asia (despite the embassy of Aristomenidas)
q: The Thebans however cried off like the Athenians, declining their aid.

s: Cleonymus is a son of Cleomenes
q: there was a dispute who should be king between Cleonymus the son of Cleomenes and Areus the son of Acrotatus.

s: Thebans attacked Agesilaus (at the sacrifice at Aulis)
q: But as he was sacrificing some Thebans attacked him, and threw the thigh-bones of the victims that were burning off the altar, and drove him out of the temple.

s: Agesilaus defeated Tissaphernes (near the Hermus in Lydia)
q: And fighting a battle with Tissaphernes, the satrap of Ionia, in the plain near the river Hermus, Agesilaus defeated the Persian cavalry and infantry

s: Agesilaus became commander of fleet (after his success by land)
q: the Lacedæmonians, delighted at the success of Agesilaus by land, readily made him leader of the fleet also.

s: Artaxerxes hears the victorious progress of Agesilaus
q: when Artaxerxes heard of the victorious progress of Agesilaus

s: Artaxerxes executed Tissaphernes (after Agesilaus’s victories)
q: he condemned Tissaphernes to death

s: Tithraustes opposed Lacedæmonians (strongly)
q: a longheaded fellow and very able man, who greatly disliked the Lacedæmonians.

s: Corinthian War began with invasion of Bœotia (by the Lacedæmonians)
q: what is known to history as the Corinthian war began with this march into Bœotia of the Lacedæmonians

s: Corinthian War compelled Agesilaus (to return his army from Asia Minor)
q: and compelled Agesilaus to bring his army home from Asia Minor.

s: Areus is a son of Acrotatus
q: there was a dispute who should be king between Cleonymus the son of Cleomenes and Areus the son of Acrotatus.

s: Agesilaus defeated Thebans (and their allies at Coronea)
q: And Agesilaus having routed their cavalry marched through Thessaly, and then through Bœotia, having conquered the Thebans and their allies at Coronea.

s: Battle of Coronea was won by Agesilaus (against the Thebans and their allies)
q: having conquered the Thebans and their allies at Coronea.

s: Agesilaus does not violate their sanctuary (though Agesilaus was wounded in the battle)
q: though Agesilaus was wounded in the battle, he did not for all that violate their sanctuary.

s: Spartan kingship ended with Cleomenes (son of Leonidas) (the last Agiad king at Sparta)
q: Cleomenes the son of Leonidas was the last king at Sparta

s: succession disputes concerned Cleonymus (and Areus over the Spartan kingship)
q: there was a dispute who should be king between Cleonymus the son of Cleomenes and Areus the son of Acrotatus.

s: oracle at Delphi warned against lame king (as a source of unexpected woes and war)
q: Sparta, beware, although thou art so great, Of having king o’er thee lame of one leg. For unexpected woes shall then prevail, And mortal-slaying wave of troublous war.”

s: Areus inherited Spartan kingship (instead of Cleonymus)
q: The Senate decided that to Areus the son of Acrotatus and not to Cleonymus belonged the hereditary office.

s: Cleonymus invited in Pyrrhus (against Sparta)
q: he eventually injured his country in various ways, and even went so far as to invite in Pyrrhus the grandson of Æacus.

s: Pyrrhus is a grandson of Æacus
q: to invite in Pyrrhus the grandson of Æacus.

s: Corinthians establishes Isthmian games (the exiled Corinthians with Lacedæmonian proclivities)
q: And not long afterwards those Corinthians who had been exiled for their Lacedæmonian proclivities established the Isthmian games.

s: Archidamus is a king of the Lacedæmonians (son of Agesilaus)
q: And during the reign of Archidamus, the son of Agesilaus, the Phocians seized the temple of Apollo at Delphi.

s: Phocians seizes Delphi (by seizing the temple of Apollo)
q: And during the reign of Archidamus, the son of Agesilaus, the Phocians seized the temple of Apollo at Delphi.

s: Phocians intends to kill young men at Delphi (after seizing the temple)
q: The Phocians intended to kill all the young men at Delphi, and to sell the women and children into slavery, and to raze the city to its foundations: all this Archidamus successfully deprecated.

s: Archidamus prevents destruction of Delphi (by deprecating the Phocians’ intended massacre and enslavement)
q: The Phocians intended to kill all the young men at Delphi, and to sell the women and children into slavery, and to raze the city to its foundations: all this Archidamus successfully deprecated.

s: Theopompus states Archidamus (received a share of the money at Delphi)
q: And Theopompus, the son of Damasistratus, said that Archidamus also had a share of the money at Delphi

s: Archidamus dies Italy (fighting the barbarians near Tarentum)
q: And he afterwards crossed over into Italy, to assist the people of Tarentum in a war with their barbarian neighbours: and he was slain there by the barbarians

s: Agis dies fighting the Macedonians and Antipater
q: And Agis, the elder son of this Archidamus, met his death fighting against the Macedonians and Antipater.

s: Eudamidas rules Lacedæmonians (as the younger son; during his reign the Lacedæmonians enjoyed peace)
q: During the reign of Eudamidas the younger one the Lacedæmonians enjoyed peace.

s: Corinthians joins Argives (the Corinthians who had remained in Corinth)
q: those who were at this time in Corinth remained there from fear of Agesilaus, but when he broke up his camp and returned to Sparta, then they also joined the Argives at the Isthmian games

s: Sparta is also called Laconia (the city was originally called Sparta)
q: On going forward from Thornax, you come to the city which was originally called Sparta, but afterwards Lacedæmon, which was once the name of the whole district.

s: Laconia is name of whole district (before becoming the later name of the city)
q: On going forward from Thornax, you come to the city which was originally called Sparta, but afterwards Lacedæmon, which was once the name of the whole district.

s: market-place of Sparta contains Spartan Senate (a council chamber for the Senate)
q: At Sparta there is a handsome market-place, and a council chamber for the Senate, and public buildings in the market-place for the Ephors and guardians of the laws, and for those who are called the Bidiæi.

s: Artemisia joins Xerxes (in the expedition against Greece; voluntarily)
q: who they say of her own accord joined Xerxes in the expedition against Greece, and displayed great valour in the sea fight at Salamis.

s: Lacedæmonians buries Agesilaus (with greater honours than any of their kings)
q: And the Lacedæmonians, when they got his dead body, buried it with greater honours than they had shewn to any of their kings.

s: Cæsar has temple at market-place of Sparta (as the first Roman who aimed at Autocracy and established the present régime)
q: two temples in the market-place, one to Cæsar, who was the first of the Romans that aimed at Autocracy, and established the present régime

s: Tisamenus is a Iamide (a native of Elis)
q: This Agias was the son of Agelochus, the son of Tisamenus. This last was a native of Elis of the family of the Iamidæ

s: Tisamenus wins five victories in war (after interpreting the oracle as referring to war)
q: And Tisamenus had his five victories, first at Platæa against the Persians, and secondly at Tegea in a battle between the Lacedæmonians and the people of Tegea and the Argives.

s: Destinies have temple at Sparta (near the tomb of Orestes)
q: the Destinies have a temple at Sparta, near to which is the tomb of Orestes the son of Agamemnon

s: Orestes has tomb at Sparta (near the temple of the Destinies)
q: the Destinies have a temple at Sparta, near to which is the tomb of Orestes the son of Agamemnon

s: Polydorus has effigy at Sparta (near the tomb of Orestes)
q: And near the tomb of Orestes is an effigy of Polydorus the son of Alcamenes

s: Polydorus appears on government seal (the Lacedæmonian public seal)
q: that the government seal all their public documents with Polydorus’ image.

s: Agesilaus comes again to Corinth (with an army)
q: And Agesilaus came again to Corinth with an army: and, as the festival of Hyacinthus was coming on, he sent home the natives of Amyclæ, to go and perform the customary rites to Apollo and Hyacinthus.

s: Odysseus wins race for the suitors of Penelope (proposed by Icarius)

s: Talthybius has tomb at Sparta (near Hellenium)

s: Castor has temple at Sparta (over his monument near Scias)

s: Proserpine has temple at Sparta (opposite the temple of Olympian Aphrodite)

s: Agesilaus assists Ætolians (against the Acarnanians)

s: Hera has temple at Sparta (on a hill near Colona; said to have been erected by Eurydice)

s: Hyperchirian Hera has temple at Sparta (built after the Eurotas overflowed the country)
q: And the temple of Hyperchirian Hera was built according to the oracle, when the Eurotas overflowed a considerable part of the country.

s: Agesilaus assists Egyptians (against the great king)

s: Agesilaus dies on the passage home (as an old man)
q: And he died on the passage home, for he was now quite an old man.

s: Amyclæ performs rites for Apollo (at the festival of Hyacinthus)
q: he sent home the natives of Amyclæ, to go and perform the customary rites to Apollo and Hyacinthus.

s: Athenians attacks This detachment (under Iphicrates)

s: bridges into Platanistas provide access to Platanistas (two bridges)

s: Lycurgus legislated for fights of the youths (as well as for the state generally)

s: Spartan youths sacrifice to Enyalius (each division sacrifices a puppy dog by night before fighting)

s: Spartan youths practice tame boars (after sacrificing; the boars are pitted together to fight)

s: Aphrodite is depicted with fetters (on her feet in the upper shrine)

q: Here is erected a temple of Athene called Poliuchus and Chalciœcus.
